title: Singular owners and possessive endings review
focus: Retrieve the eight taught rules with one or several owned things.
targetSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Translate “minun kissani” into English.
exercises.explanation: Minun identifies my ownership; kissa means “cat”.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: First- and second-person possessive endings: form or meaning confused

exercises.prompt: Write “This is your house.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Address one person. Use talo (“house”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -si identifies your ownership.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Sinun is the personal owner form of sinä; it selects -si.
talo (“house”) + -si = talosi. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -si: use talosi.
Keep the possessive ending -si even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Sinun needs -si; changing the ending changes the owner.
